# Meerschaum Documentation

> Craft elegant data pipes with Meerschaum.

## Home
- [Home](https://meerschaum.io/): Want to use Meerschaum in your code? Check out the <a href="https://docs.meerschaum.io">package documentation</a>!

## Get Started
- [🛠️ Setup](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/): Run Meerschaum commands with mrsm (or python -m meerschaum if ~/.local/bin/ isn't in your PATH).
- [🏗️ Building a Pipe](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/bootstrap/): Pipes fetch and sync data from connectors. For this example, we will be using the connector plugin:noaa from the data plugin noaa. Type the commands below to bootstrap an example pipe.
- [📦️ Compose Projects](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/compose-projects/): Now that you've got the idea behind pipes, let's write our own plugins and put together a project using <a href="/reference/compose">Meerschaum Compose</a>.
- [🖥️ Web Console](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/start-api/): You can use Meerschaum from its web interface. From within a mrsm shell, type to commands below to see how:

## Reference
- [📚 Meerschaum Reference Wiki](https://meerschaum.io/reference/): So you've just completed the Getting Started guide ― congratulations! 🥳 "What's next?", you might ask.
- [🚰 Pipes](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/): A Meerschaum pipe represents a data stream into a table and the necessary parameters to sync new data.
- [🥾 Bootstrapping](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/bootstrapping/): The bootstrap pipes action includes a setup wizard to guide you through the process of creating new pipes. In this tutorial, we'll be looking at the prompts you'll encounter to help you better underst
- [📥 Syncing](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/syncing/): I wrote my master's thesis on comparing syncing strategies. Here are the presentation slides which summarize my findings.
- [📖 Reading Data](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/reading/): Use Pipe.getdata() and its convenience wrappers to read rows from the instance.
- [🔖 Tags](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/tags/): You can define custom groupings of pipes with tags. Consider the example below:
- [🧩 Parameters](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/parameters/): This page catalogs useful keys in the parameters dictionary.
- [🔤 Data Types](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/dtypes/): This page explains what Meerschaum data types (dtypes) are, when to use each one, and how dtype coercion behaves during syncs. For the dtype table in context with the rest of the metadata, see paramet
- [🧹 Maintenance](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/maintenance/): Over time a pipe's target table accumulates dead rows, stale planner statistics, and uncompressed history. Meerschaum provides a family of maintenance actions to keep tables lean and queries fast. Eac
- [🔒 Access and Locks](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/access-and-locks/): Meerschaum is open by default. On an instance where nobody sets up teams, access or locks, every
- [🕸️ Pipelines](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/): > New in v5. The Syncing Engine understands how your pipes depend on one another. It decides which pipes need to run, how wide each sync must be, runs independent branches in parallel, and records wha
- [🗃️ Engine State](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/state/): The engine adds no database files to your root directory. Everything it remembers lives on your instance, as internal pipes alongside Meerschaum's own tables (on flavors that have schemas, PostgreSQL 
- [♾️ Continuous Mode](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/continuous/): mrsm sync pipes --loop keeps the engine running. On a flat selection it behaves exactly as v4's laps did: every selected pipe syncs, then the process sleeps --min-seconds N after the lap ends, then th
- [📊 Visualization](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/visualization/): The engine emits one typed event per transition, and everything you see is drawn from that stream or from the recorded run:
- [🔌 Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/): Meerschaum coordinates everything via connectors. Use cases for Connectors include fetching and inserting data when syncing pipes.
- [🗂️ SQL Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/sql-connectors/): Meerschaum's first-class connector is the SQLConnector. Several built-in sql connectors are defined by default:
- [🗄️ Instance Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/instance-connectors/): Instance connectors store pipes' metadata (and may also be used as a source connector, e.g. the #!python SQLConnector).
- [🗝️ Valkey Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/valkey/): The ValkeyConnector syncs pipes to a Valkey instance. Valkey is an in-memory key-value store forked from Redis, so the same connector also works against a Redis server.
- [❓ Other Connector Types](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/other-connectors/): Though the SQL Connector is the premier Meerschaum connector type, there are plenty of other implementations of the instance connector interface.
- [🐍 Python API](https://meerschaum.io/reference/python-api/): Most of this documentation is written from the perspective of the mrsm command-line interface, but everything you can do from the CLI you can also do from Python. This page is a practical cheat sheet 
- [🥞 Stack](https://meerschaum.io/reference/stack/): The Meerschaum stack is an integrated collection of services designed to help you start visualizing your data as quickly as possible.
- [⬆️ Upgrading the Stack](https://meerschaum.io/reference/stack-upgrades/): Pulling newer images (mrsm stack pull, or mrsm upgrade mrsm) updates the stack's software, but
- [🌐 API Instance](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/): The Meerschaum API instance (and Web Console) lets you manage pipes, jobs, and connectors over the Internet. Start the API server with the stack or via start api; see Deployment below for ways to run 
- [Security and Tokens](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/tokens/): Meerschaum tokens are long-lived API keys that grant programmatic access to a Meerschaum instance. They are a secure way to authenticate for services like IoT devices or CI/CD pipelines without using 
- [Permissions and Rate Limits](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/permissions/): An API server decides three things about every request: whether the route is served at all (route groups), who may call it (authentication and scopes), and how often (rate limits). All of it lives und
- [Pipelines, Access and Actions over HTTP](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/routes/): Besides the existing pipe, user, token, plugin and job routes, an API server has routes for saved Pipelines, their runs, teams and pipe access and the console's background actions. Existing route bodi
- [NGINX](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/nginx/): Hosting Meerschaum behind NGINX is a great way set up TLS/SSL with Let's Encrypt (certbot), especially when several sites share port 443. (The API server can also serve HTTPS by itself: see TLS / SSL 
- [Web Console](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/web-console/): The Meerschaum Web Console provides a graphical interface for managing your Meerschaum instance, served by the API instance. To access it, start the API (mrsm start api) and navigate to your host URL 
- [🤖 MCP Server](https://meerschaum.io/reference/mcp/): Meerschaum ships a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI agent can discover your pipes, read their data, and run actions without you writing any glue code.
- [Tool Reference](https://meerschaum.io/reference/mcp/tools/): Every tool, resource, and prompt the MCP server exposes, generated
- [Security](https://meerschaum.io/reference/mcp/security/): The MCP server hands an AI agent the same capabilities a person has at the CLI or web console. Treat a token for it exactly as you would a Meerschaum login.
- [🎼 Compose](https://meerschaum.io/reference/compose/): Meerschaum Compose does the same for Meerschaum as Docker Compose does for Docker: you can consolidate everything into a single YAML file ― including all of the pipes and configuration needed for your
- [⏯️ Actions](https://meerschaum.io/reference/actions/): Run mrsm help (or mrsm -h) to see every action with a one-line description, then the options.
- [📺 Watch and Shell Shortcuts](https://meerschaum.io/reference/actions/watch/): show prints something once; watch keeps it on screen as it changes. watch run and watch jobs are full-screen views (new in v5) that take the whole terminal and give it back as it was when you leave; w
- [👥 Teams, Access and Locks](https://meerschaum.io/reference/actions/teams-and-access/): Meerschaum is open by default: on an instance where nobody sets up teams, access or locks, every
- [👷 Background Jobs](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/): Meerschaum's job management system lets you run any process in the background ― just add -d to any command. Thanks to the built-in scheduler, you no longer have to worry about manually configuring cro
- [🔧 Data Analysis Tools](https://meerschaum.io/reference/data-analysis-tools/): Meerschaum comes with a pre-configured data visualization stack so that you can spend your time on analysis rather than configuring servers.
- [➕ Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/): Meerschaum plugins let you ingest any data source into pipes as well as defining custom actions, connectors, API endpoints, dash apps, and more.
- [✍️ Writing Your Own](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/writing-plugins/): Rust plugins can be a single .rs file for actions, data sources, or connectors. See the Rust quickstart to get started, or the advanced guide for packaging and the full SDK. The examples below use Pyt
- [🤔 Types of Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/types-of-plugins/): > This page introduces the different types of Meerschaum plugins. For technical information, consult the Writing Your Own Plugins tutorial.
- [🖥️ Web Pages and Routes](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/web-pages/): Plugins add pages to the Web Console with #!python @webpage, make them interactive with Dash callbacks, and add API routes with #!python @apiplugin. This page covers who may use them (signed-in visito
- [🗃️ Caching](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/caching/): Some things are slow to compute: a query over a big table, a chart, a call to someone else's API. meerschaum.utils.cache remembers the result for a while, shares it with every process of your deployme
- [🧪 Testing Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/testing/): meerschaum.testing is a pytest plugin: your tests get a throwaway Meerschaum root, a fresh SQLite instance for each test, pipes that clean up after themselves, the web API in the test process and the 
- [🦀 Rust Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/rust-plugins/): A Rust plugin can be one .rs file. Add a command, return rows of data, or create a

- [🚀 Repositories](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/repositories/): Meerschaum gives you the ability to easily install and create plugins. Refer to the guide below on how to install, write, and publish plugins.
- [🌳 Environment Variables](https://meerschaum.io/reference/environment/): You can manage the behavior of Meerschaum and emulate multiple installations with environment variables.
- [🩺 Troubleshooting](https://meerschaum.io/reference/troubleshooting/): A symptom-driven guide to the most common Meerschaum issues. Each entry follows Symptom → Cause → Fix.
- [⬆️ Migrating to v5](https://meerschaum.io/reference/migrating-to-v5/): Meerschaum v5 is a rewrite of the core, the CLI, jobs, compose, the HTTP API and the MCP server in Rust. The web console stays the Plotly Dash app of v4, served by the Python package. The meerschaum P
- [📖 Glossary](https://meerschaum.io/reference/glossary/): This page defines the core Meerschaum domain terms in one place. Each entry links to its reference documentation where one exists. Other pages can deep-link to any term by its heading anchor, e.g. #up
- [💼 Portable](https://meerschaum.io/reference/meerschaum-portable/): The standalone "portable" archive (mrsm-full- / mrsm-minimal-, built with pyoxidizer) is no longer produced. This page remains so old links keep working.
